title: The Measure of the Man
subtitle: How America Remembers T.R.
intro: A face on a mountain, a park with his name on it, a toy bear in every nursery, and a permanent place near the top of the historians' rankings. Fifteen questions on what Roosevelt left behind, and how the country decided to remember him.
heroAlt: James Earle Fraser's equestrian statue in front of the Roosevelt Memorial, New York City
heroCredit: Fraser statue of T.R. in front of Roosevelt Memorial, New York City. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

badge.title: The Measure of the Man
badge.shareText: I scored {score}/{total} on the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library's Legacy quiz — {tier}. Try it:

questions.prompt: Roosevelt is one of four presidents carved on Mount Rushmore. Who are the others?
questions.explanation: Washington, Jefferson and Lincoln — and Roosevelt, the only twentieth-century figure and by far the most recent. The sculptor Gutzon Borglum chose him partly for the Panama Canal and partly because he had known him.
questions.imageAlt: The Fraser equestrian statue in front of the Roosevelt Memorial, New York
questions.credit: Fraser statue of T.R. in front of Roosevelt Memorial, New York City. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: Where do historians typically rank Roosevelt among American presidents?
options: In the middle of the pack
Consistently in or near the top five
Rankings vary wildly with no pattern
questions.explanation: He appears in or near the top five in almost every scholarly survey since such rankings began, usually alongside Lincoln, Washington and Franklin Roosevelt. His position has been remarkably stable across decades of changing historical fashion.
questions.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt in his private office
questions.credit: Theodore Roosevelt, 26th President of the United States, in his private office. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

questions.prompt: Which everyday object is named after Roosevelt?
questions.explanation: The teddy bear, from the 1902 Mississippi hunt where he refused to shoot a bear that had been tied up for him. A Brooklyn shopkeeper made a stuffed bear, called it Teddy's bear, and an industry followed. Roosevelt disliked the nickname and tolerated the toy.
questions.imageAlt: Berryman's cartoon "Drawing the Line in Mississippi"
questions.credit: "Drawing the Line in Mississippi," Clifford K. Berryman. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

questions.prompt: What phrase did Roosevelt coin for the presidency as a platform for persuasion?
questions.explanation: "Bully" meant excellent in his usage, not domineering. He meant the presidency gave him a magnificent platform from which to preach — and he used it more deliberately than any president before him.
questions.credit: "A young head on old shoulders." Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

questions.prompt: Which part of Roosevelt's record is most often called his most enduring?
questions.explanation: Roughly 230 million acres protected — national forests, monuments, parks and bird reserves. Much of it is still public land today, and the legal machinery he used is still being used and argued over.
questions.credit: Amidst America's noblest scenery — President Roosevelt on Glacier Point. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

questions.prompt: How did Roosevelt himself explain what made his career possible?
options: His years in the North Dakota Badlands
questions.explanation: He credited North Dakota. He told his biographer Hermann Hagedorn that it was there the romance of his life began — and the Library now standing in Medora exists because he said so.
questions.credit: Theodore Roosevelt on the round-up, 1885. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: What did Vice President Thomas Marshall say when Roosevelt died in his sleep?
options: That the country had lost its conscience
That death had to take him sleeping, or there would have been a fight
questions.explanation: Marshall remarked that death had to take Roosevelt sleeping, because if he had been awake there would have been a fight. It is the most quoted line about him and it captures the public image exactly.
questions.credit: The Parlor, Sagamore Hill. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

questions.prompt: Which political tradition claims descent from Roosevelt's later programme?
options: The Progressive movement in both major parties
Neither; his ideas died with him
questions.explanation: The New Nationalism of 1910 and the Bull Moose platform of 1912 proposed things — a minimum wage, social insurance, regulation of industry — that both parties later adopted in different forms. Politicians across the spectrum still quote him, which tells you something about how broad his appeal remains.
questions.imageAlt: Roosevelt and Hiram Johnson after the Progressive Party nomination
questions.credit: Roosevelt and Johnson after nomination. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

questions.prompt: Roosevelt's Medal of Honor was awarded when?
questions.explanation: In 2001, more than a century after the fact. He was recommended for it in 1898 and the award was blocked, largely because he had publicly criticised the War Department's handling of the campaign.
questions.imageAlt: The monument on San Juan Hill
questions.credit: The monument on San Juan Hill. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: The Roosevelts produced a second president. Who, and what was the relation?
options: Franklin Roosevelt, a distant cousin who married Theodore's niece
questions.explanation: Franklin Delano Roosevelt was a distant cousin from the Hyde Park branch, and married Theodore's niece Eleanor in 1905 — with Theodore giving the bride away. The two branches were of different parties and did not always get along.
questions.credit: Roosevelt family portrait. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: What distinction does Theodore Roosevelt National Park hold?
options: The only national park named for a single person
questions.explanation: It is the only one named for an individual. It covers three units in the North Dakota Badlands, including the Elkhorn Ranch site where his cabin stood.
questions.imageAlt: The Little Missouri River in the Badlands
questions.credit: "A plains river" — the Little Missouri. Photograph by Theodore Roosevelt. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: Roosevelt was the first American to win a Nobel Prize in any category. Which one?
questions.explanation: The Peace Prize, in 1906, for mediating an end to the Russo-Japanese War. He gave the money away. Two later presidents — Wilson and Carter — also won it, and Obama received it in office.
questions.imageAlt: The Nobel Peace Prize certificate awarded to Theodore Roosevelt
questions.credit: Certificate of the Nobel Prize. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: How do historians today treat the harder parts of Roosevelt's record?
options: They are examined alongside his achievements — his views on race, Native nations and empire caused lasting harm
They are considered irrelevant to his presidency
questions.explanation: An honest account includes both. His beliefs about race and his conduct toward Native nations and in the Philippines did real and lasting damage, and the Library presents that plainly rather than around it.
questions.imageAlt: The Fraser equestrian statue in front of the Roosevelt Memorial
questions.credit: Fraser statue of T.R. in front of Roosevelt Memorial, New York City. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: What happened to the equestrian statue that stood outside the American Museum of Natural History?
options: It was removed in 2022 and relocated
questions.explanation: James Earle Fraser's statue showed Roosevelt mounted with a Native American man and an African man on foot beside him — a composition widely read as a hierarchy. It was removed in 2022 and sent on long-term loan to the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in Medora.
questions.imageAlt: The Fraser equestrian statue in front of the Roosevelt Memorial, New York City
questions.credit: Fraser statue of T.R. in front of Roosevelt Memorial, New York City. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: When did the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library open?
questions.explanation: July 4, 2026, in Medora — 107 years after his death, in the Badlands he credited with making him. It is a working presidential library built where the story turned rather than where he governed.
questions.credit: Medora in 1883 — the office and company store of the Marquis de Mores. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.
